newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Solel Boneh raises 83 mln shekel in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Solel Boneh raises 83 mln shekel in IPO.

text.p: The initial public offering in Israel's Solel Boneh, a construction company, sold at its maximum 920 shekel price and raised 82.8 million shekels, underwriters said on Wednesday citing preliminary figures.
The offering was oversubscribed by 45 times, with orders totalling 3.7 billion shekels, said a spokesman for Leader Securities Underwriting.
About half the offering had been taken up earlier in an institutional tranche, which also sold for the top price.

The offering comprised 90,000 units comprising shares, convertible bonds and two series of warrants. The bonds are convertible in the years 2000-2003. One warrant series is convertible by November 20 and the other on May 20, 1999.

The share component gives the public 9.9 percent of equity, but the figure rises to 42.1 percent when fully diluted. Shikun U'Binui Holdings, which is controlled by the Histadrut labour federation, holds the remainder of the shares.
Another 2.5 million warrants will be sold separately on Thursday for an expected price of 10 to 13 shekels, leader said.
